title: AlphaOPT: Formulating Optimization Programs with Self-Improving LLM Experience Library

problem.claim: Automating optimization modeling requires translating natural-language descriptions into precise mathematical formulations and executable solver code.

gap.claim: Existing approaches have limited generalization, and systematic acquisition, refinement, and reuse of experience in structurally constrained settings remains unclear.

contributions.claim: AlphaOPT is a self-improving experience library that learns optimization modeling knowledge from limited supervision without requiring gold-standard programs or parameter updates.
AlphaOPT uses a continual two-phase cycle that extracts solver-verified insights from failed attempts and refines their applicability using aggregate cross-task evidence.
The design supports reusable modeling principles, transfer across problem instances, and bounded library growth.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On multiple optimization benchmarks, performance increased from 65% to 72% as training items increased from 100 to 300.
AlphaOPT outperformed the strongest baseline by 9.1% and 8.2% on two out-of-distribution datasets.
The authors characterize structured experience learning grounded in solver feedback as a practical alternative to retraining for complex formulation and execution tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Optimization modeling is difficult to automate because natural-language descriptions must become precise formulations and executable solver code.
Prompting and retraining approaches generalize poorly, while systematic experience reuse remains unresolved.
AlphaOPT learns and evolves a library of solver-verified modeling insights through a continual two-phase cycle.
The library is intended to support reusable principles, transfer, and bounded growth.
The authors report improvement with more training data and gains over the strongest baseline on two out-of-distribution datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method extracts structured insights from failed attempts and refines their applicability using aggregate evidence across tasks.

interpretation.claim: Separating experience extraction from experience evolution may help maintain reusable reasoning knowledge under changing task evidence.

application.claim: For structured generation tasks, store solver- or evaluator-grounded lessons and periodically revise their applicability across tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond optimization modeling or other structurally constrained reasoning tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark names, task sizes, evaluation protocol, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details of library extraction, evolution, or bounded growth.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
